about: Football's defaults, as data (docs/PLAN-start-a-game-gpt.md track L, L1): a sport's standard scoring, categories, lineup slots and locks, and the game specs a sport's Make it a game starts from instead of asking the bot. Stat keys are Football's (src/lib/sports/football.ts): players' and a team defense's in one table, since a key is unique in the sport (a quarterback's interceptions thrown are INT, a defender's DINT, a team defense's DSTINT). The team defense is one line per side (Yahoo's DEF: football.ts's defenseId), its points allowed in Yahoo's brackets (PA0 a shutout ... PA35). Slots take its positions or position groups (ESPN's roster says PK for a kicker). The specs are in the game spec's shape (A1's schema, on the engine branch); slots and categories aren't in that schema yet (L4 adds them), so they're kept beside it for the spec to read.
finalSource: Step 2.7 (docs/PLAN-sports-ready.md): the final a game through the playoffs runs to, as people name it ("Through the Super Bowl"); words for 4.0's pass

scoring.source: Yahoo's default league scoring, half-PPR (help.yahoo.com/kb/SLN6489.html): offense, then kickers, then the team defense; 25 passing yards a point, 10 rushing or receiving yards a point, fractions kept

categories.source: Yahoo's football leagues score points, not categories: none by default

slots.source: Yahoo's default roster: QB, 2 WR, 2 RB, TE, a W/R/T flex, K, DEF and 6 bench (15)

ir.source: Yahoo's default roster's 2 IR, outside its 15; its football IR takes IR, O (Out) and PUP (and NFI, which ESPN's rosters don't list); not Q, D or suspended (help.yahoo.com/kb/SLN6489.html, SLN6425.html, 2026-11-20)

waivers.source: Yahoo's football defaults: a continual rolling list, weekly waivers, no maximum acquisitions (help.yahoo.com/kb/SLN6489.html, 2026-11-20). Here a week's claims open when the week before has its results and run the day before its first game; free agents after that until the week's last game starts (docs/PLAN-sports-ready.md step 2.5)

pace.source: The user's rule (2026-11-19, BACKLOG 218): a seat at its own pace is never more than one game behind; when the next game starts, the one before counts as watched (docs/PLAN-sports-ready.md step 2.6)

season.about: A season-long league: draft a full roster, set a lineup each week, play someone head to head each week.

short.about: One game, a team's next few or a week's slate: everyone drafts a few players, every one of them scores, most points wins.

pickem.about: Each game, before it starts: who wins? A point for each one right, most points wins (a tie counts for nobody).

pickAFew.about: Each game, before it starts: pick three players. 3 points for each one who has the most receiving yards in the game (tied, each of them), most points wins.

ask.ask: Pick three: who has the most receiving yards?

bestBall.about: Best ball: draft a full roster and never set a lineup: each game, your best nine count, most points wins.

squares.about: Squares on each game (the Super Bowl's party game): take squares on a 10-by-10 grid of the two scores' last digits, the digits drawn at random once everyone has theirs. The square of the score wins a point at the end of each of the first three quarters and two for the final score, most points wins.

playoffs.source: Yahoo's and ESPN's fantasy seasons, playoffs and all, end at Week 17, the regular season's last week before Week 18's, when teams rest their starters (BACKLOG 214 and 226, the user's calls of 2026-11-19 and 11-20): a game scored by players' stats on the regular season ends there unless its maker says otherwise, and its playoffs end there whatever its span

season.about: A season-long league: draft a full roster, set a lineup each week, play someone head to head each week, and the top two meet in a final in Week 17.

bracket.about: A playoff bracket: before the NFL playoffs start, pick who wins every game, round by round to the Super Bowl. A point for each one right in the first round, doubling each round after it; most points wins.

ask.ask: Who wins every game of the NFL playoffs?
